properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored Crypto++ 5.6.1 ships the DES-EDE3 implementation (Sweet32-vulnerable 64-bit block cipher) with no Armory application call site found. The one urllib3 site is live TLS configuration: DEFAULT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST of the vendored urllib3 1.8 pyOpenSSL adapter, applied to every wrapped socket via ctx.set_cipher_list (pyopenssl.py:397), keeps ECDH+3DES/DH+3DES/RSA+3DES as fallback suites on Armory's HTTPS update-download path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored Crypto++ 5.6.1 ships a complete RC4 (ARC4) stream cipher implementation in the CppBlockUtils binary Armory links against. No call site in Armory's own application code was found, but the cipher is compiled into the shipped library and reachable through Crypto++'s registered factories. Presence is the inventory fact: the shipped image carries RC4 whether or not the app calls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Crypto++ OID registry makes AES-128 in all four modes available to anything using the vendored library's ASN.1/algorithm infrastructure. In the urllib3 adapter, ECDH+AES128 is the preferred cipher strength of the live DEFAULT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST — the AES-128 floor on Armory's HTTPS fetch path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live TLS cipher configuration of the vendored urllib3 1.8: AES-GCM suites are the top preference for every pyOpenSSL-wrapped HTTPS socket. The strongest part of this 2013-era default list; the key exchanges named in those suites (ECDHE/DHE/RSA) remain Shor-vulnerable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The engine's SHA-512 surface; the SHA-512 workhorse of this codebase is the C++ KdfRomix wallet KDF (CryptoPP::SHA512, cppForSwig/EncryptionUtils.cpp), with this Python wrapper mirroring it for the engine and the unit test pinning wrapper-vs-C++ equivalence. SHA-512 meets CNSA 2.0.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OID table = Crypto++ 5.6.1 library surface. UI strings = the user-facing label of Armory's wallet at-rest encryption; the actual implementation chain (AES-256-CFB via Crypto++, random IV from AutoSeededX917RNG<AES>, key from the KdfRomix KDF) lives in cppForSwig/EncryptionUtils.cpp:298-360 called from armoryengine/PyBtcAddress.py:545/272/582/615, and is filed as a separate finding because no deterministic object covers those lines. Cipher-list site = ECDH+AES256 preferred in the vendored urllib3

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The only TLS sessions in this tree. Default posture of the vendored stack: resolve_ssl_version(None) returns PROTOCOL_SSLv23 (auto-negotiation, no minimum version); resolve_cert_reqs(None) returns CERT_NONE, so certificate verification is OFF unless a caller explicitly requests it; and Armory's local edit (connection.py:190-204) replaced match_hostname with a hardcoded subjectAltName allowlist ['bitcoinarmory.com','scripts.bitcoinarmory.com']. PQ status: undecided at scan time — governed by whic

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored Crypto++ 5.6.1 ships the PKCS#12 password-based KDF (the KDF that protects .p12/.pfx keystores), exercised with SHA-1 as the PRF in the library self-test. Shipped library surface; no Armory code handles or derives PKCS#12 keys, so the practical exposure is library-only.
